decision_frictions.name: Cardiology vs Nephrology
decision_frictions.topic: Medication restart timing (sacubitril/valsartan, spironolactone, empagliflozin, furosemide, carvedilol)
decision_frictions.cardiology_position: Preserve HFrEF/CAD protection; decompensation/readmission risk if protective therapy is lost.
decision_frictions.nephrology_position: Renal recovery, potassium, blood pressure reserve, intake, and volume status remain fragile.
decision_frictions.balance: Both clinically defensible; correct path defines monitored sequencing with parameters that gate each restart (creatinine/eGFR trajectory, potassium, BP, intake/weight).

decision_frictions.name: Family vs Primary Team
decision_frictions.family_position: Baseline-informed observation that 'better than Monday' is not the same as ready to manage without support.
decision_frictions.primary_team_position: Objective improvement and plausible discharge planning.
decision_frictions.balance: Correct pathway integrates both; family observations are baseline-informed collateral, not anxiety to reassure away.

decision_frictions.name: Endocrinology vs Primary Team
decision_frictions.endocrinology_position: Chronic steroid exposure and taper uncertainty are clinically relevant; monitoring and teaching priority.
decision_frictions.primary_team_position: Cautious about over-attributing improvement-lag to steroids after sepsis-oriented treatment helps.
decision_frictions.balance: Endocrine concern is real but adrenal insufficiency is NOT established; do not over-call.

traps.name: Visible discharge snapshot overtrust / Visible-but-incomplete plan
traps.conceal_surface: EW22 (discharge_facing_plan_snapshot_05232026.docx) is a one-page reassuring summary: improvement narrative, anticipated 2026-05-24 discharge, follow-up list, simplified medication framing. Coherent and professional.
traps.reveal_surface: EW22 DELIBERATELY OMITS: unresolved restart decisions, functional and cognitive concerns from EW17-EW19, family-baseline observations from EW20, prednisone reconciliation. Correct posture is to use EW22 as a source to reconcile, NOT as the synthesis.

traps.name: Premature or delayed HF/AKI restart
traps.conceal_surface: Cardiology and Nephrology each have time-qualified positions across dated addenda 2026-05-19 through 2026-05-23.
traps.reveal_surface: Correct path balances both positions and defines monitored sequencing with parameters (creatinine/eGFR, potassium, BP, intake/weight) gating each restart.

traps.name: Prednisone source error
traps.conceal_surface: Multiple disagreeing sources: patient, family, medication bag/label, pharmacy fills, rheumatology intent.
traps.reveal_surface: Use rheumatology (EW6) as highest outpatient taper-intent source while integrating med rec, pharmacy, family, and patient recollection. Keep dose/taper uncertainty EXPLICIT. NO numeric dose anywhere.

traps.name: Inpatient-only therapy drift
traps.conceal_surface: MAR (EW13) shows inpatient correctional insulin lispro and other inpatient-only actions on the same grid as continued chronic therapy.
traps.reveal_surface: Do NOT convert inpatient correctional insulin (or other inpatient-only MAR actions) into outpatient medications on the discharge list without independent discharge justification.

traps.name: Buried medication-management capacity evidence
traps.conceal_surface: OT (EW19), nursing (EW17), family (EW20) findings are buried in routine notes and not synthesized anywhere.
traps.reveal_surface: Integrate OT, nursing, and family findings into teach-back and supervision planning, not just the medication list.

traps.name: Sepsis-anchor carry-forward / Copy-forward diagnosis closure
traps.conceal_surface: EW2 (ED provider) and EW3 (admission H&P) reasonably frame suspected urinary-source sepsis. EW12 shows improvement of infection markers.
traps.reveal_surface: Preserve reasonable initial frame while showing why later weakness, medication decisions, steroid history, and disposition still mattered. Do NOT let infection frame narrate full course.

traps.name: Consultant chronology flattening / Latest-note authority bias
traps.conceal_surface: Cardiology, Nephrology, Endocrinology consult addenda span 2026-05-19 through 2026-05-23.
traps.reveal_surface: Summarize consultant input by TIMING and clinical context. Each recommendation is time-qualified. Most recent does NOT equal most authoritative.

traps.name: Functional evidence omission
traps.conceal_surface: Functional and cognitive evidence sits in PT, OT, nursing, family observations — easy to skip in favor of physician summaries.
traps.reveal_surface: Include these observational sources when describing course, readiness, follow-up, and safety risk.

traps.name: Medical stability equals readiness
traps.conceal_surface: Improved infection markers, renal trajectory toward baseline, intake recovery, mental-status improvement (EW12) imply readiness.
traps.reveal_surface: Reconcile trajectory with PT/OT gaps (EW18, EW19), nursing evening confusion (EW17), family baseline-informed concerns (EW20), CM/SW service requirements (EW21).

traps.name: Family-concern dismissal / minimization
traps.conceal_surface: Family voice can be characterized as generic resistance or anxiety.
traps.reveal_surface: Treat Mara Merrow's observations as baseline-informed longitudinal collateral; weighed against the visible plan, not minimized.

traps.name: Service-plan overconfidence and disposition siloing
traps.conceal_surface: Case management note lists services and equipment options.
traps.reveal_surface: Equipment, home health, education, transportation, caregiver capacity must be CONFIRMED rather than assumed. Integrate with medical plan.

traps.name: Consultant winner selection
traps.conceal_surface: Cardiology, Nephrology, Endocrinology each have authoritative voices.
traps.reveal_surface: Do NOT automatically defer to any one service; synthesize timing, trends, patient status.

traps.name: Steroid overcall (adrenal insufficiency as hidden answer)
traps.conceal_surface: Endocrinology identifies steroid exposure and taper-uncertainty as relevant.
traps.reveal_surface: Endocrinology explicitly does NOT declare adrenal insufficiency established. Rheumatology documents intended taper without verifying adherence. Do NOT make adrenal insufficiency the hidden single explanation.

traps.name: Invented follow-up or outcome facts (Tasks 5 and 6)
traps.conceal_surface: Tasks 5 (2026-05-31, +7) and 6 (2026-06-23, +30) use post-discharge anchors as review points.
traps.reveal_surface: World record ends EW22 on 2026-05-23 18:00. NO post-discharge file exists. Do NOT invent: new symptoms, labs, vitals, visits, recovery, deterioration, readmission, non-readmission, adverse events, or blame narrative.

traps.name: Medication monitoring gap
traps.conceal_surface: Trend flowsheet (EW12) shows trends without a scheduled post-discharge monitoring plan.
traps.reveal_surface: Identify renal function, potassium, BP symptoms, volume, intake, diabetes therapy, HF/CAD sequencing as follow-up priorities at +7.

traps.name: Friction collapse (Task 6)
traps.conceal_surface: Friction can be 'resolved' by picking a winner or pretending all agreed.
traps.reveal_surface: Preserve defensible positions from family, primary team, Cardiology, Nephrology, Endocrinology; identify safety implications of each unresolved friction.

self_containment_principle: Every claim in a task's correct answer must be traceable to the task prompt + task-level files + world-level files. If a clinical fact, date, diagnosis, or regulatory finding cannot be accounted for by those sources, it is either fabrication (if asserted as fact) or must be acknowledged as uncertain. Supplementary files add realism and background but never carry sole critical evidence.
world_summary: Korvin Merrow presents a familiar but unforgiving inpatient transition: an older, medically complex patient improves after admission, yet safe discharge remains genuinely uncertain. The world tests whether a reviewer can separate medical stabilization from discharge readiness by synthesizing source reliability, consultant timing, medication actions, objective trends, bedside function, and family baseline knowledge. The trap architecture works because the most visible documents are the most reassuring, while decisive evidence sits in less prominent sources: a polished discharge snapshot, evolving consultant addenda, an unresolved prednisone record, and buried nursing and therapy observations.
